title: Highly Efficient and Effective LLMs with Multi-Boolean Architectures
claim: At comparable memory budgets, our low-bit Boolean-kernel models reach lower perplexity than quantized baselines and trade off size versus quality more favorably.
layout: single plot, perplexity versus model size, three colored curves with distinct markers
description: A single line plot with a grid. The x-axis is Model Size in GB, from 0 to about 12.5. The y-axis is Perplexity on C4, with a down arrow showing lower is better, and runs from about 12 to 42. Three curves with distinct markers: orange circles, blue pentagons, and green triangles. The orange curve starts very high, about 42 perplexity at tiny size, then falls steeply to about 17 at around 3 GB. The blue curve extends furthest right, to about 12.5 GB, and ends near 12.5 perplexity. The green curve sits mostly lowest and leftmost, running from about 29 at tiny size down to about 12 at about 3 GB. The green curve forms the lower-left Pareto frontier, so it gives the best quality for a given size. There is no legend in the crop.
caption: Finetuning OPT mod- els (Zhang et al., 2022) using our 3 Boolean kernels ( ), com- pared to OPTQ (Frantar et al., 2023) ( ), which quantizes the models to 3 bits, and the FP16 baseline ( ) on the C4 dataset.
abstract: Weight binarization has emerged as a promising strategy to reduce the complexity of large language models (LLMs). Existing approaches fall into post-training binarization, which is simple but causes severe performance loss, and training-aware methods, which depend on full-precision latent weights, adding complexity and limiting efficiency. We propose a novel framework that represents LLMs with multi-kernel Boolean parameters and, for the first time, enables direct finetuning LMMs in the Boolean domain, eliminating the need for latent weights. This enhances representational capacity and dramatically reduces complexity during both finetuning and inference. Extensive experiments across diverse LLMs show our method outperforms recent ultra low-bit quantization and binarization techniques.
